title: Passive and impersonal forms
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Passive voice: ser + particípio with an agent
lessons.explanation: The passive is ser + past participle, and the participle agrees in gender and number with the subject: a casa foi construída, os livros foram comprados. The agent follows por, which contracts with the article: pelo, pela, pelos, pelas. The auxiliary ser carries the tense (é construída, foi construída, será construída, tinha sido construída). Use it when the receiver of the action is the topic and the agent is secondary. Do not leave the participle invariable (a casa foi construído is wrong) and do not drop the auxiliary (a casa construiu pelos operários is wrong).

examples.en: The house was built by the workers.

examples.en: The letters are written by him.

lessons.title: Passive se and indeterminate se
lessons.explanation: Se can build two different structures. With a transitive verb it is the passive se (se apassivadora), and the verb agrees with the thing acted on: vendem-se casas, aluga-se quarto, fazem-se cópias. With a verb that has no direct object, usually one that takes a preposition, it is the indeterminate se, and the verb stays in the third person singular whatever follows: precisa-se de funcionários, trata-se de um erro, reclama-se de problemas. In standard writing, do not use a singular verb with a plural object (vende-se casas is wrong) and do not pluralise the verb with a prepositional complement (precisam-se de funcionários is wrong).

examples.en: Houses are sold on this street.

lessons.title: Estar + particípio: resulting state versus ser + particípio
lessons.explanation: Ser + participle describes the event or process: a porta foi fechada pelo vento. Estar + participle describes the state that results: a porta está fechada. The participle agrees with the subject in both: as luzes estavam apagadas, as janelas estão abertas. Choose by what you mean: if someone did it, use ser; if you are describing how things are, use estar. An agent phrase fits ser (a porta foi fechada pelo vento) and is unnatural with estar. Do not use ser for a current state: a loja é fechada agora is wrong, a loja está fechada agora is right.

lessons.title: Impersonal third person: dizem que, diz-se que
lessons.explanation: To report what is said or done without naming who does it, Portuguese uses the third person plural with no subject: dizem que ele vai viajar, falam que o prefeito vai renunciar, roubaram minha bolsa. It also uses se with the verb in the singular before a que clause: diz-se que o prédio é antigo, acredita-se que a crise acabou. Use these when the agent is unknown, general or unimportant. Do not use the first person plural (dizemos) for an unnamed group, and do not pluralise se before que (dizem-se que is wrong).

lessons.title: Double participles: regular and short forms
lessons.explanation: Some verbs have two participles: a regular one in -ado or -ido and a short irregular one. Aceitar gives aceitado and aceito; entregar gives entregado and entregue; ganhar gives ganhado and ganho; gastar gives gastado and gasto; pagar gives pagado and pago; eleger gives elegido and eleito; prender gives prendido and preso; matar gives matado and morto; expulsar gives expulsado and expulso. In the passive with ser or estar, use the short form and agree it with the subject: a conta foi paga, o ladrão foi preso, os alunos foram expulsos. The regular form appears with ter and haver in formal writing (tinham entregado), though Brazilian speakers also use the short form there. Do not use the regular form in the passive: foi prendido is wrong.
